audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 14, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, medical, and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for childhood illness, disguised maternal journey, Ahijah's blindness and age, dynastic extermination, corpse desecration, child death, collective mourning, exile theology, Rehoboam, anti-LGBTQ translation misuse, Egyptian invasion, sacred treasure loss, and continual war.

verses.restored: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became sick.

familiar.text: At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

modern.text: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill,

original.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא חָלָ֖ה אֲבִיָּ֥ה בֶן יָרָבְעָֽם

verses.restored: Jeroboam said to his wife, Please arise and disguise yourself so they will not know you are Jeroboam's wife, and go to Shiloh. Look, Ahijah the prophet is there, who spoke concerning me that I would be king over this people.

familiar.text: And Jeroboam said to his wife, Arise, I pray thee, and disguise thyself, that thou be not known to be the wife of Jeroboam; and get thee to Shiloh: behold, there is Ahijah the prophet, which told me that I should be king over this people.

modern.text: and Jeroboam said to his wife, “Now get up, disguise yourself so they will not recognize you as my wife, and go to Shiloh. For Ahijah the prophet is there; it was he who spoke about my kingship over this people.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יָרָבְעָ֜ם לְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ ק֤וּמִי נָא֙ וְהִשְׁתַּנִּ֔ית וְלֹ֣א יֵֽדְע֔וּ כִּי אתי אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְהָלַ֣כְתְּ שִׁלֹ֗ה הִנֵּה שָׁם֙ אֲחִיָּ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא הֽוּא דִבֶּ֥ר עָלַ֛י לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Take in your hand ten loaves, cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what shall happen to child.

familiar.text: And take with thee ten loaves, and cracknels, and a cruse of honey, and go to him: he shall tell thee what shall become of the child.

modern.text: Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will become of the boy.”

original.text: וְלָקַ֣חַתְּ בְּ֠יָדֵךְ עֲשָׂרָ֨ה לֶ֧חֶם וְנִקֻּדִ֛ים וּבַקְבֻּ֥ק דְּבַ֖שׁ וּבָ֣את אֵלָ֑יו ה֚וּא יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔ךְ מַה יִּֽהְיֶ֖ה לַנָּֽעַר

verses.restored: Jeroboam's wife did so. She arose, went to Shiloh, and came to house of Ahijah. Ahijah could not see, for his eyes had become fixed/dim because of age.

familiar.text: And Jeroboam’s wife did so, and arose, and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. But Ahijah could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age.

modern.text: Jeroboam’s wife did as instructed; she arose and went to Shiloh and arrived at Ahijah’s house. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were dim because of his age.

original.text: וַתַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֔ם וַתָּ֨קָם֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁלֹ֔ה וַתָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֣ית אֲחִיָּ֑ה וַאֲחִיָּ֨הוּ֙ לֹֽא יָכֹ֣ל לִרְא֔וֹת כִּ֛י קָ֥מוּ עֵינָ֖יו מִשֵּׂיבֽוֹ

verses.restored: YHWH said to Ahijah, Look, wife of Jeroboam is coming to inquire from you concerning her son, for he is sick. Thus and thus you shall speak to her. When she comes, she will make herself a stranger.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Ahijah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to ask a thing of thee for her son; for he is sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her: for it shall be, when she cometh in, that she shall feign herself to be another woman.

modern.text: But the LORD had said to Ahijah, “Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. You are to say such and such to her, because when she arrives, she will be disguised.”

original.text: וַיהוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל אֲחִיָּ֗הוּ הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֡ם בָּאָ֣ה לִדְרֹשׁ֩ דָּבָ֨ר מֵעִמְּךָ֤ אֶל בְּנָהּ֙ כִּֽי חֹלֶ֣ה ה֔וּא כָּזֹ֥ה וְכָזֶ֖ה תְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֑יהָ וִיהִ֣י כְבֹאָ֔הּ וְהִ֖יא מִתְנַכֵּרָֽה

verses.restored: When Ahijah heard sound of her feet as she entered doorway, he said, Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you make yourself a stranger? I am sent to you with a hard message.

familiar.text: And it was so, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another? for I am sent to thee with heavy tidings.

modern.text: So when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet entering the door, he said, “Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised? For I have been sent to you with bad news.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲחִיָּ֜הוּ אֶת ק֤וֹל רַגְלֶ֨יהָ֙ בָּאָ֣ה בַפֶּ֔תַח וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֹּ֖אִי אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּ֗ה אַ֚תְּ מִתְנַכֵּרָ֔ה וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י שָׁל֥וּחַ אֵלַ֖יִךְ קָשָֽׁה

verses.restored: Go, say to Jeroboam: Thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: Because I raised you from midst of people and made you leader over my people Israel,

familiar.text: Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,

modern.text: Go, tell Jeroboam that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I raised you up from among the people and appointed you ruler over My people Israel.

original.text: לְכִ֞י אִמְרִ֣י לְיָרָבְעָ֗ם כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֛עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲרִימֹתִ֖יךָ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָעָ֑ם וָאֶתֶּנְךָ֣ נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: tore kingdom from house of David and gave it to you, yet you were not like my servant David, who kept my commands and walked after me with all his heart, doing only upright in my eyes,

familiar.text: And rent the kingdom away from the house of David, and gave it thee: and yet thou hast not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, and who followed me with all his heart, to do that only which was right in mine eyes;

modern.text: I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you. But you were not like My servant David, who kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes.

original.text: וָאֶקְרַ֤ע אֶת הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד וָאֶתְּנֶ֖הָ לָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא הָיִ֜יתָ כְּעַבְדִּ֣י דָוִ֗ד אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁמַ֨ר מִצְוֺתַ֜י וַאֲשֶׁר הָלַ֤ךְ אַחֲרַי֙ בְּכָל לְבָב֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת רַ֖ק הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָֽי

verses.restored: but did evil beyond all before you, and went and made for yourself other gods and cast images to provoke me, and cast me behind your back,

familiar.text: But hast done evil above all that were before thee: for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back:

modern.text: You have done more evil than all who came before you. You have proceeded to make for yourself other gods and molten images to provoke Me, and you have flung Me behind your back.

original.text: וַתָּ֣רַע לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁר הָי֣וּ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֡לֶךְ וַתַּעֲשֶׂה לְּךָ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים אֲחֵרִ֤ים וּמַסֵּכוֹת֙ לְהַכְעִיסֵ֔נִי וְאֹתִ֥י הִשְׁלַ֖כְתָּ אַחֲרֵ֥י גַוֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: therefore look, I am bringing evil upon house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every male—literally, one who urinates against wall—both restrained and abandoned in Israel, and sweep away remnant of house of Jeroboam as one sweeps dung until it is gone.

familiar.text: Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.

modern.text: Because of all this, behold, I am bringing disaster on the house of Jeroboam: I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both slave and free, in Israel; I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as one burns up dung until it is gone!

original.text: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא רָעָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י לְיָֽרָבְעָם֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֔יר עָצ֥וּר וְעָז֖וּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבִֽעַרְתִּי֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית יָרָבְעָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְבַעֵ֥ר הַגָּלָ֖ל עַד תֻּמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: One belonging to Jeroboam who dies in city dogs shall eat, and one who dies in field birds of heavens shall eat, for YHWH has spoken.

familiar.text: Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat: for the LORD hath spoken it.

modern.text: Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.’ For the LORD has spoken.

original.text: הַמֵּ֨ת לְיָֽרָבְעָ֤ם בָּעִיר֙ יֹאכְל֣וּ הַכְּלָבִ֔ים וְהַמֵּת֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יֹאכְל֖וּ ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר

verses.restored: You, arise and go to your house. When your feet enter city, child shall die.

familiar.text: Arise thou therefore, get thee to thine own house: and when thy feet enter into the city, the child shall die.

modern.text: As for you, get up and go home. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.

original.text: וְאַ֥תְּ ק֖וּמִי לְכִ֣י לְבֵיתֵ֑ךְ בְּבֹאָ֥ה רַגְלַ֛יִךְ הָעִ֖ירָה וּמֵ֥ת הַיָּֽלֶד

verses.restored: All Israel shall mourn for him and bury him, for he alone of Jeroboam shall come to grave, because in him something good toward YHWH, Divine of Israel, was found in house of Jeroboam.

familiar.text: And all Israel shall mourn for him, and bury him: for he only of Jeroboam shall come to the grave, because in him there is found some good thing toward the LORD God of Israel in the house of Jeroboam.

modern.text: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. For this is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will receive a proper burial, because only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam.

original.text: וְסָֽפְדוּ ל֤וֹ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְקָבְר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כִּֽי זֶ֣ה לְבַדּ֔וֹ יָבֹ֥א לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם אֶל קָ֑בֶר יַ֣עַן נִמְצָא ב֞וֹ דָּבָ֣ר ט֗וֹב אֶל יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּבֵ֥ית יָרָבְעָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH shall raise for YHWH-self a king over Israel who shall cut off house of Jeroboam that day—and what? Even now.

familiar.text: Moreover the LORD shall raise him up a king over Israel, who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day: but what? even now.

modern.text: Moreover, the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day—yes, even today!

original.text: וְהֵקִים֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֥וֹ מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַכְרִ֛ית אֶת בֵּ֥ית יָרָבְעָ֖ם זֶ֣ה הַיּ֑וֹם וּמֶ֖ה גַּם עָֽתָּה

verses.restored: YHWH shall strike Israel as reed shakes in water, uproot Israel from this good land given to their ancestors, and scatter them beyond River, because they made their Asherah poles, provoking YHWH.

familiar.text: For the LORD shall smite Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water, and he shall root up Israel out of this good land, which he gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the river, because they have made their groves, provoking the LORD to anger.

modern.text: For the LORD will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land that He gave their fathers, and He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking the LORD to anger.

original.text: וְהִכָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנ֣וּד הַקָּנֶה֮ בַּמַּיִם֒ וְנָתַ֣שׁ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵ֠עַל הָאֲדָמָ֨ה הַטּוֹבָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַן֙ לַאֲב֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וְזֵרָ֖ם מֵעֵ֣בֶר לַנָּהָ֑ר יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ אֶת אֲשֵׁ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם מַכְעִיסִ֖ים אֶת יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: YHWH shall give Israel up because of sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and made Israel sin.

familiar.text: And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin.

modern.text: So He will give Israel over on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit.”

original.text: וְיִתֵּ֖ן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּגְלַ֞ל חַטֹּ֤אות יָֽרָבְעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Jeroboam's wife arose, went, and came to Tirzah. As she came to threshold of house, child died.

familiar.text: And Jeroboam’s wife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah: and when she came to the threshold of the door, the child died;

modern.text: Then Jeroboam’s wife got up and departed for Tirzah, and as soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.

original.text: וַתָּ֨קָם֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֔ם וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ וַתָּבֹ֣א תִרְצָ֑תָה הִ֛יא בָּאָ֥ה בְסַף הַבַּ֖יִת וְהַנַּ֥עַר מֵֽת

verses.restored: They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to word of YHWH spoken by hand of servant Ahijah the prophet.

familiar.text: And they buried him; and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by the hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.

modern.text: And they buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the prophet. Nadab Succeeds Jeroboam

original.text: וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וַיִּסְפְּדוּ ל֖וֹ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַד עַבְדּ֖וֹ אֲחִיָּ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא

verses.restored: Rest of acts of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, look, they are written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel.

familiar.text: And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he waged war and how he reigned, they are indeed written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יָֽרָבְעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְחַ֖ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מָלָ֑ךְ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Days Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years. He lay with his ancestors, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And the days which Jeroboam reigned were two and twenty years: and he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And the length of Jeroboam’s reign was twenty-two years, and he rested with his fathers, and his son Nadab reigned in his place. Rehoboam Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 12:13–14)

original.text: וְהַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָלַ֣ךְ יָרָבְעָ֔ם עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם שָׁנָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ נָדָ֥ב בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign and reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, city YHWH chose from all tribes of Israel to put name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

familiar.text: And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD did choose out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.

modern.text: Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.

original.text: וּרְחַבְעָם֙ בֶּן שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה בֶּן אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וְאַחַ֣ת שָׁנָה֩ רְחַבְעָ֨ם בְּמָלְכ֜וֹ וּֽשֲׁבַ֨ע עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֣ה מָלַ֣ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הָ֠עִיר אֲשֶׁר בָּחַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָשׂ֨וּם אֶת שְׁמ֥וֹ שָׁם֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נַעֲמָ֖ה הָעַמֹּנִֽית

verses.restored: Judah did evil in eyes of YHWH and provoked YHWH to jealousy by sins they committed, beyond all their ancestors had done.

familiar.text: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins which they had committed, above all that their fathers had done.

modern.text: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and by the sins they committed they provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוּדָ֛ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְקַנְא֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ מִכֹּל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבֹתָ֔ם בְּחַטֹּאתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָֽאוּ

verses.restored: They also built for themselves high places, standing stones, and Asherah poles upon every high hill and beneath every green tree.

familiar.text: For they also built them high places, and images, and groves, on every high hill, and under every green tree.

modern.text: They also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

original.text: וַיִּבְנ֨וּ גַם הֵ֧מָּה לָהֶ֛ם בָּמ֥וֹת וּמַצֵּב֖וֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים עַ֚ל כָּל גִּבְעָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה וְתַ֖חַת כָּל עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן

verses.restored: There were also male cult personnel/consecrated persons in land. They acted according to all detestable practices of nations YHWH dispossessed before children of Israel.

familiar.text: And there were also sodomites in the land: and they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the LORD cast out before the children of Israel.

modern.text: There were even male shrine prostitutes in the land. They imitated all the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites. Shishak Raids Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 12:1–12)

original.text: וְגַם קָדֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֣ה בָאָ֑רֶץ עָשׂ֗וּ כְּכֹל֙ הַתּוֹעֲבֹ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: In fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem:

modern.text: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיְהִ֛י בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֖ית לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֑ם עָלָ֛ה שושק מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: He took treasures of house of YHWH and treasures of king's house; he took everything. He also took all gold shields Solomon made.

familiar.text: And he took away the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king’s house; he even took away all: and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

modern.text: He seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields that Solomon had made.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת אֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֶת הַכֹּ֖ל לָקָ֑ח וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת כָּל מָגִנֵּ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה

verses.restored: King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and entrusted them to hands of commanders of guard who kept doorway of king's house.

familiar.text: And king Rehoboam made in their stead brasen shields, and committed them unto the hands of the chief of the guard, which kept the door of the king’s house.

modern.text: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ רְחַבְעָם֙ תַּחְתָּ֔ם מָגִנֵּ֖י נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְהִפְקִ֗יד עַל יַד֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרָצִ֔ים הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים פֶּ֖תַח בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Whenever king went to house of YHWH, guards carried them and returned them to guardroom.

familiar.text: And it was so, when the king went into the house of the LORD, that the guard bare them, and brought them back into the guard chamber.

modern.text: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would bear the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.

original.text: וַיְהִ֛י מִדֵּי בֹ֥א הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה יִשָּׂאוּם֙ הָֽרָצִ֔ים וֶהֱשִׁיב֖וּם אֶל תָּ֥א הָרָצִֽים

verses.restored: Rest of acts of Rehoboam and all he did—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Judah?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, along with all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י רְחַבְעָ֖ם וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

familiar.text: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

modern.text: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.

original.text: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֧ה בֵין רְחַבְעָ֛ם וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָ֖ם כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: Rehoboam lay with his ancestors and was buried with ancestors in City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. Abijam his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess. And Abijam his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David; his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite. And his son Abijam reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב רְחַבְעָ֜ם עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֤ר עִם אֲבֹתָיו֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נַעֲמָ֖ה הָעַמֹּנִ֑ית וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲבִיָּ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

translation_notes: Jeroboam's unnamed wife travels in disguise while carrying fear for a sick child and the political risk of her husband's identity. Her grief and constrained agency must remain visible.
Ahijah's blindness is attributed to age, not sin or lack of discernment. Blindness must not be moralized, mocked, or treated as automatic supernatural compensation.
The child is called good and is mourned by all Israel. His death must never be preached as deserved punishment for a parent's wrongdoing.
The oracle threatens extermination of a dynasty and exposure of bodies to dogs and birds. This is collective punishment and corpse desecration, not an ethical model.
The idiom 'one who urinates against wall' is contemptuous male-targeting language and should not become a masculinity test.
Uprooting and scattering are interpreted through covenant failure. This may not be used to blame displaced, colonized, exiled, or refugee communities for their suffering.
Verse 24 uses qadesh, likely referring to male cult personnel or consecrated persons. Rendering it with a modern sexuality label has fueled anti-LGBTQ abuse and is philologically irresponsible.
Naamah's Ammonite identity is repeated without proving foreign motherhood caused Judah's conduct. Ethnicity is not moral inheritance.
Shishak's seizure of temple and palace treasure exposes how quickly Solomon's gold spectacle becomes war booty. Bronze replacements preserve appearances after material loss.
Continual war between the two kings means ongoing cost to civilians, workers, soldiers, and border communities.
safety_note: Do not blame a child, mother, blind elder, foreign woman, LGBTQ people, religious minorities, or displaced communities for royal failure. Do not celebrate dynastic extermination or corpse desecration. Center the sick child, the mother's journey, communal mourning, and the human cost of war.
